title: Distribution and Sharing Controls
summary: Documents report distribution expectations, data handling rules, and cross-team handoff patterns.
coverage: Service desk linkage and tracking completeness
Data sensitivity handling for exported reports

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Reports may include sensitive vulnerability evidence and infrastructure context. Treat every exported PDF as controlled security material.

sections.title: Distribution model in RAPTOR
paragraphs: RAPTOR currently provides controlled generation, storage, download, and deletion for report files. It does not provide built-in email dispatch or external recipient workflows.
Distribution to stakeholders is performed outside RAPTOR after download. Teams should enforce local policy for classification, encryption, and approved transfer channels.

sections.title: Access control matrix
paragraphs: Every report file operation is controlled by permission decorators plus record-level assignment enforcement. This protects report material from cross-assignee access by default.

sections.title: Pre-send checks for stakeholder delivery
paragraphs: Before sharing any report externally, validate that the report reflects current operational truth and includes traceability links for remediation follow-up.
orderedList: Confirm pentest status and assignee are current.
Verify vulnerability and remediation flags are accurate.
Ensure service desk link is populated for downstream tracking.
Regenerate report after final save to avoid stale narrative or findings.
Review the downloaded PDF for template correctness and data leakage risk.
Record where and to whom the report was distributed.

sections.title: Retention and replacement semantics
paragraphs: Both manual and generated reports are stored as file references in `pentest_data`. File names are unique and decoupled from user-facing naming conventions.
When pentest data is deleted by an admin, RAPTOR attempts to remove both `report_file` and `generated_report_file` from storage.
